query: How do you actually forgive yourself?
why_in_two_sentences: Greater Good leads with a gripping true story and twelve research-based steps; Healthline offers twelve medically reviewed tips. Both are numbered-list pages, and ours beats them on mechanism: the judgment on the act stays while the daily punishment gets reassigned, including the case both competitors skip, when the person is dead, gone, or will not speak to you.
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Separates the judgment on what you did from the punishment you administer daily, and gives that punishment a different job
Explains why deciding to feel differently never holds, and why the guilt returns hardest when life finally goes well
Covers self-forgiveness when amends are impossible (the person is dead, gone, or no-contact)
Distinguishes real accountability from guilt wearing accountability's clothes
34 verbatim FAQs on the mechanics competitors leave vague

above_the_fold.ours: H1 is the query, the short answer gives the judgment-vs-punishment split in four sentences, then recognition sentences; the answer arrives before any scrolling.
above_the_fold.theirs: Greater Good opens with a multi-paragraph true story of a man who lost his family to a gambling addiction; slower to the answer but emotionally gripping, with Berkeley/Stanford provenance visible.

questions_they_answer_that_we_dont: Is it healthy to forgive yourself?
trust_signals: Greater Good carries Berkeley's Greater Good Science Center brand and a Stanford course anecdote; Healthline shows a named writer and PhD medical reviewer; ours has no byline, institution, or citations.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: Surface a compact numbered sequence (name what you did, make the amends that are makable, reassign the punishment); both competitors' numbered steps are their main scannability advantage on a how-do-I query.
